summary: DEFLATE (RFC 1951) and gzip (RFC 1952) in pure Mojo — no FFI, no dependencies.
description:
`deflate` compresses, `inflate` decompresses, and `inflate_at` decompresses
one stream out of several laid back to back, reporting where it ended.
`gunzip` decodes a `.gz` file (every member, CRC-32 and length checked),
`gunzip_at` one member of it, and `gzip` writes one.

```mojo
from deflate import deflate, inflate

var packed = deflate(Span(data))    # List[UInt8], raw DEFLATE
var back = inflate(Span(packed))    # List[UInt8], == data
```

`inflate` and `deflate` streams are *raw*: no zlib (RFC 1950) header, no
gzip wrapper, no trailing checksum. Avro's `deflate` block codec is raw and
needs nothing more; gzip files go through `gunzip`.

modules.summary: gzip (RFC 1952) framing over the raw DEFLATE in `raw.mojo`.
modules.description:
`gunzip` decodes a whole `.gz` file: every member of a concatenated stream,
each one's header (all five flags: FTEXT, FHCRC, FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT)
parsed and skipped, and each one's CRC-32 and ISIZE checked against what it
decoded to. `gunzip_at` decodes one member and reports where it ended, as
`inflate_at` does for raw streams. `gzip` writes a single member.

The CRC-32 is the zlib/gzip one (reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320), slice-by-8
as in hashes.mojo's `crc32`. It is repeated here rather than imported so the
tin keeps no sibling dependency: a consumer still needs nothing but
`-I deflate.mojo/src`.

overloads.summary: `armv8-crc` or `slice-by-8`: which CRC-32 this build uses.
Decompress a gzip file: all of its members, concatenated.
overloads.description:
Each member's CRC-32 and length are verified. Zero bytes after the last
member are padding (as gzip(1) and Python's `gzip` accept); anything else
there raises, as does an empty input.

overloads.signature: def gunzip_at(data: Span[UInt8], mut end: Int) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Decompress the one gzip member at the start of `data`, verifying its CRC-32 and length, and set `end` to the offset just past its trailer.
overloads.description:
For walking a multi-member file one member at a time, so only one
member's output is held at once:

```mojo
var pos = 0
while pos < len(data):
    var end = 0
    var part = gunzip_at(Span(data)[pos:], end)
    pos += end
```

overloads.signature: def gzip(data: Span[UInt8], level: Int = Int(6)) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Compress `data` into a single gzip member.
overloads.description:
`level` 0 writes stored (uncompressed) DEFLATE blocks; 1 to 9 all use
`deflate`'s one fixed-Huffman strategy, so they produce the same bytes.
The header carries no name, comment or timestamp (MTIME 0, OS 255).

modules.summary: Raw DEFLATE (RFC 1951) — `inflate` and `deflate`, in pure Mojo.
modules.description:
*Raw* DEFLATE is the compressed stream on its own: no zlib (RFC 1950) header,
no gzip (RFC 1952) wrapper, no trailing checksum. A caller that needs one of
those framings parses it itself and hands the body here — Avro's `deflate`
block codec is raw already, and Parquet's `GZIP` codec is this plus a gzip
header and trailer.

Implementing it rather than binding zlib keeps the tin free of FFI and of any
sibling dependency, so a consumer needs nothing but `-I ../deflate.mojo/src`.

`inflate` handles all three block types (stored, fixed-Huffman,
dynamic-Huffman). `deflate` emits fixed-Huffman blocks from a single-slot
hash-chain LZ77 matcher — the same "fast" strategy `snappy.mojo` uses —
which keeps the encoder small.

overloads.signature: def inflate_at(data: Span[UInt8], mut end: Int) -> List[UInt8]
overloads.summary: Decompress a DEFLATE stream, and report where it ended.
overloads.description:
`end` is set to the offset of the first byte *after* the stream, rounded
up to a byte boundary. Callers with several streams back to back —
concatenated gzip members, for instance — need it to find the next one;
callers that do not can use `inflate`.

overloads.summary: Compress to a raw DEFLATE stream (one fixed-Huffman block).
